admin-controls.md:
# Admin control centre

Open Settings → Page tools → Admin control centre, or More → Team tools and help on a phone.

Needs attention shows missing pit reports, completed-match reports, current responsible scouts, permanent-owner context, unowned teams, conflicts, handoffs and practice progress.

Scouting by team shows a compact grid of team numbers and names. Search by name/number, filter by status, or use Previous teams / Next teams instead of scrolling a long match list. Phones show six teams per page; larger screens show twelve. Green means no outstanding warnings: pit and completed-match reports are present, or an Admin explicitly dismissed the missing evidence. Yellow means pit coverage is present or dismissed but completed matches are missing. Red means pit evidence is missing and not dismissed. An unavailable schedule is labelled unknown, never fully scouted. Future matches are pending, not missed.

Select a team to see its permanent owner, pit scout, missed matches and the responsible scout for each match, including accepted handoffs. Admins and Owners can use Dismiss team warnings to clear both pit and currently missed-match warnings, turning the tile green when the schedule is available. This never creates a report or changes analytics or server-confirmed duty totals. Restore team warnings reverses the dismissal. Individual matches also retain dismiss/restore controls. Dismissed evidence remains labelled as missing inside the detail window. Changes persist across reloads and are recorded in Activity. Newly completed unscouted matches raise warnings again. Stale changes are rejected; refresh and review rather than overwriting another admin's work.

Duty totals, unowned teams, conflicts, handoff history and practice progress remain available in collapsed sections below the grid. The default view concentrates on team status.

Members manages ordinary membership. Only Owners can promote/demote Admins or offer ownership transfer.

Assignments manages permanent owners and explicit duties. Reassignment changes responsibility and is recorded; review existing accepted coverage before making changes.

Forms and reports links to existing form builders and report search. Archive forms to retain historical definitions. Removing a report requires a reason and can be reversed. Removed IDs remain reserved so an offline retry cannot resurrect a removed report.

Reports using an unrecognized historical form snapshot are retained for review, not silently discarded or included in analytics. Inspect them and use the reasoned review action to approve legitimate historical evidence.

Shared data controls which structured measurements Scouters can see across the team. Activity shows recorded actions and timestamps. Earlier actions are not retrospectively fabricated.

ai-analysis.md:
# Scouting calculations

Open Scouting analyst directly, or use the analyst within Analytics. Choose a suggested question, name a team, or use a configured numeric metric. Answers use deterministic calculations on your device. No generative AI, account, API key, or external request is needed.

The calculation engine uses form and question IDs rather than season rules or guessed question names. New seasons need their own forms and metric mappings, not a software update. Unsupported questions return insufficient information.

Check source reports, sample sizes, coverage, disagreements and missing counts. Pit evidence stays separate from match performance. Name teams and metrics in each question; questions do not assume conversation memory.

For automatic scoring, defense, support and reliability lists, open [Alliance strategy](alliance-strategy.md).

alliance-strategy.md:
# Alliance strategy

Open Strategy, choose or create an event picklist, and add teams from the directory. Only Admins/Owners edit shared lists; Scouters can inspect permitted data.

Use two to four selected teams for comparison. Review the same metric and units, sample size, missing data, disagreement and scouting coverage.

Move entries with the up/down buttons on touch or keyboard; drag is optional. Save to confirm the list on the server. Unsaved list drafts are preserved locally. A conflicting revision requires reviewing the saved version; it must not silently replace your edits.

Strategy notes and Needs review markers record your judgement. Pick order is not official ranking and is not a predicted match outcome.

## Automatic selection sheet

In Analytics → Metric definitions, assign each numeric field an alliance role (scoring, defense, support or reliability) and preferred direction. Save the definitions. Use fields relevant to your current game; no season-specific code update is needed.

Strategy automatically displays one sheet per role. Each field uses the average of one median per linked match, then compares teams with the same field. A category score equally averages the field percentiles, with ties shared. These are relative event scores out of 100, not game points or win probabilities. A single observed team gets 50. Teams missing any configured field remain unranked. Your own team, pit evidence and unlinked reports do not enter these rankings.

Review source reports, small samples, disagreements and coverage. Admins/Owners can use Create scoring picklist (or another category) to make a new editable draft. Review and save it to share; existing lists are preserved. The sheet recalculates as reports change, while saved picklist order stays under your control.

assignments-and-randomization.md:
# Assignments and randomization

A permanent owner receives a list of robot teams for the entire event. That scout pit scouts those teams and match scouts each scheduled appearance.

1. An Admin opens Assignments → Manage ownership.
2. Select participating scouts and the pit/match forms.
3. Choose Fill unowned teams to retain saved owners, or explicitly choose Rerandomize unlocked teams.
4. Preview team counts, allocations and collision warnings.
5. Apply the preview. A stale preview is rejected without overwriting newer work.

Team counts are balanced when unconstrained. Locked or preserved ownership can limit balance. Collision minimization is a heuristic and cannot guarantee zero conflicts.

Use Move or lock individual teams for permanent changes. Accepted handoffs and explicit match overrides are preserved. Deselection prevents new ownership; it does not silently abandon existing teams. Move those teams explicitly.

My work shows permanent teams, pit progress, next duties, conflicts and coverage. Pending upload is not server-confirmed completion. Schedule refresh reconciles new duties without duplicating them.

events-and-history.md:
# Events and history

The active event is shared across your workspace. Admins manage it in Settings → Events. The top bar displays the active event and has no switch control.

Changing events preserves reports, schedules, assignments, handoffs, photos and picklists. Forms stay available. Older clients with a destructive switch dialog must reload before switching.

My Team and scouting use the configured event rather than replacing it with the next event from Blue Alliance. If no event is configured, ask an Admin to activate one.

Use Settings → Browse event history for read-only team profiles, comparison and permitted evidence from saved events without changing the active event. The report library can also search historical reports. Delayed authorized reports retain their original event when they synchronize. Previously cleared records cannot be reconstructed automatically; consult your backups.

handoffs-and-breaks.md:
# Handoffs and breaks

Use Request cover on a match assignment, or open that match and choose Handoff for the robot.

Select a connected teammate who has no robot in that match. You remain responsible until they accept. They can decline; you can cancel a pending offer.

Offers expire after five minutes or at the scheduled/predicted match start, whichever is sooner. Handoffs close when the match starts. Unknown start times do not permit a handoff. Both peers must be connected when required; push delivery is not acceptance.

Acceptance changes one robot in one match only. Permanent team ownership and other matches remain unchanged. A confirmed matching report completes the handoff. Admins can inspect pending, accepted, declined, cancelled, expired and completed history.

For a short break covering multiple matches, request each required match explicitly; there is no silent event-wide transfer.

internals.md:
# Internal architecture

The deployed entry is Clasue-scout-app/src/main.jsx → frc-scout-local.jsx. React/Vite serves a PWA; Express server.cjs owns authorization and JSON persistence.

Canonical team_allocations store permanent owners. assignments store effective pit/match duties. Accepted handoffs update a single duty and append responsibility_history. Legacy event.assignment is a compatibility mirror, not a second editable owner source.

The database migration is additive, retains unknown fields, and creates a pre-upgrade backup before the first write. JSON mutations use one process and synchronous writes/rename. Do not run multiple independent application writers against one file.

Audit entries are stored with mutations and contain operational metadata, not passwords, API keys, report answers or images. submission_states records reversible removal; original submission IDs stay immutable.

IndexedDB scout-device-v1 retains cache/queue/drafts/meta/receipts. Practice queue entries use the practice endpoint; existing real report payloads and draft keys remain compatible.

All profile/comparison/analyst/export calculations use analytics.js. Blue Alliance and Match13 keys are private server settings. Run npm test and npm run build in Clasue-scout-app. Browser tests run only against temporary local fixtures.

match-scouting.md:
# Match scouting

1. Open Assignments or the match schedule.
2. Choose a robot assigned to you in that match.
3. Confirm the event, team, match, alliance and form.
4. Record observed answers. Missing information is not zero.
5. Submit, then check upload status.

You can scout only your assigned robot or accepted coverage. If two owned teams play simultaneously, request one-match cover before the match starts. An Admin can review unresolved coverage.

Match keys identify playoff sets as well as match numbers. Do not manually reuse another match's draft context. Saved drafts with different context are preserved and show a warning.

notes-and-photos.md:
# Notes and robot photos

Pit and match forms already support notes and robot photos. Open a team profile for observations, pit evidence, confidence and source reports. Each observation retains its report context.

Use labelled observations rather than inventing conclusions from missing data. Capture useful robot views without unnecessary personal information. Photos are compressed on the phone and remain in the offline report queue until acknowledged.

Raw notes/photos follow report permissions. Scouter shared summaries publish structured measurements only. A separately curated shared gallery and external media migration remain a later roadmap item; do not assume private photos are public.

offline-and-sync.md:
# Offline and synchronization

Before a competition, open Argus online, sign in and choose Device and sync → Sync & prepare device. Wait for the app shell and downloaded data to be ready.

Drafts, queued reports and receipts are stored in IndexedDB on the original device/account/workspace. A report is complete only after server confirmation. Lost acknowledgements retry the same immutable ID instead of creating duplicates.

Keep the browser's site data. Do not clear storage to fix an update while reports are pending. Export pending reports first. One conflicting report must not prevent unrelated uploads.

Handoffs and administration require a server connection. Cached role information never grants backend permission. Reconnect, sign in if needed, review rejected uploads and refresh data after role changes.

App updates invalidate read caches without deleting drafts or queued reports.

pit-scouting.md:
# Pit scouting

Open My assignments and choose Pit scout for a team. Use the assigned pit form, record observations, then submit.

Draft answers save automatically on this phone. Submission first saves a local queued report; check Device and sync for server confirmation.

A pit visit marker and a pit report are different. Marking a visit does not complete a required pit report. Undoing a visit preserves its history and never deletes a report.

Photos and notes remain part of their original reports. Pit measurements are separate from match performance and do not inflate match coverage.

practice-and-training.md:
# Practice and training

Open Practice from More or Help. Choose a pit or match form and practice using Sample Team 9999.

The form controls, autosave and offline queue are the same mechanisms used for real scouting. Practice uses separate draft keys and a separate server collection. A visible Practice banner remains present.

Submit one pit and one match practice report to record basic progress. This is not a certification of observation accuracy. Admins can see which types have been submitted.

Practice never affects real reports, duty completion, team statistics, analyst evidence or alliance lists. Returning to real assignments preserves unfinished practice and real drafts.

reminders.md:
# Assignment reminders

Open Assignments to see next duties and conflicts. The handoff inbox displays incoming requests and status changes while Argus is open.

An upload queue is not a notification delivery guarantee. Phone sleep, lost connectivity, denied notification permission or expired requests can delay alerts. Always review assignments before a match.

Open Settings → Reminders for the in-app inbox, availability, routine reminders and optional push. Push requires HTTPS and browser permission; iPhones may require installing Argus on the Home Screen. No permission prompt appears until you choose Enable. Disabling stops this device's workspace subscription.

Routine reminders include an upcoming match, a daily incomplete-pit reminder and conflicts. Routine push is quiet from 22:00 to 07:00 in your configured timezone. Handoff status alerts remain time-sensitive. Repeated reminders are deduplicated and delivery retries are bounded. Delivery never accepts a handoff or changes responsibility. Request coverage in time for the recipient to open Argus and accept.

roles-and-permissions.md:
# Roles and permissions

Scouter is stored internally as member. Owners inherit Admin and Scouter capabilities. Admins inherit scouting capabilities.

- Scouters submit reports, view assignments, request/accept one-match handoffs, practice, and view approved shared measurements. They can read their own raw reports.
- Admins manage forms, reports, permanent ownership, coverage and ordinary Scouter membership. They cannot promote users or change Owner/Admin membership.
- Owners manage Admin roles and private integrations. Ownership transfer requires the current Owner's password and the recipient's acceptance within 15 minutes. The previous Owner becomes Admin.

The backend checks permissions on direct API requests. Removing membership preserves existing reports and local drafts, but that user cannot upload until authorized again. A role change cannot erase already observed information; downloaded reads are invalidated on a confirmed change.

setup.md:
# Setup

Use Node 22.12 or newer. The active app folder is spelled Clasue-scout-app.

1. Preserve your current database before updating.
2. Run bash scripts/install-debian.sh from the repository root as the normal installation user.
3. Sign in and create or join your team workspace.
4. Owners configure private Blue Alliance and Match13 connections in Settings.
5. Admins add and explicitly activate an event in Settings → Events.
6. Create a pit and match form, then preview permanent ownership in Assignments.
7. Each scout opens Device and sync and prepares their phone before leaving internet access.

Live data stays in ~/.local/share/scout-app/db.json, outside Git and releases. Private credentials and sessions stay beside it. The first persisted upgrade creates db.json.pre-upgrade-v1.bak; keep regular backups as well.

Restart: sudo systemctl restart scout-app

Deploy latest GitHub code: sudo systemctl start scout-update

Read logs: sudo journalctl -u scout-app -u scout-update -n 100 --no-pager

troubleshooting.md:
# Troubleshooting

Old interface: finish current work, then use Load new version. Avoid clearing browser storage when reports are pending.

No assignments: confirm the active event and ask an Admin to review permanent ownership and generated duties.

Two teams at once: request one-match cover from an eligible connected scout. If no one can accept, inform the coordinator; do not pretend both robots are covered.

Report blocked: keep the draft/queue, read its error and export it from Device and sync. Check membership, assignment, form version and report limits.

Server update failed: sudo journalctl -u scout-update -n 100 --no-pager. Check local Git changes, Node version, disk and RAM. Live data belongs outside Git. Never hard-reset a live database or overwrite newer records with an older backup.

Restart only the app: sudo systemctl restart scout-app. Check status: sudo systemctl status scout-app scout-update.timer.

Remote administration: use SSH over Tailscale; no public shell is embedded in Argus.
